title: 2011 AMC 12B Problem 9
statement: Two real numbers are selected independently at random from the interval \([-20, 10].\) What is the probability that the product of those numbers is greater than zero?

solutions.text:
The interval has length \(30,\) with \(20\) of it negative and \(10\) of it positive. So each number is positive with probability \(\dfrac13\) and negative with probability \(\dfrac23.\)

The product is positive when both are positive or both are negative: \[ \left(\dfrac13\right)^2+\left(\dfrac23\right)^2=\dfrac19+\dfrac49=\dfrac59. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The product is positive exactly when both numbers share the same sign
Each number is negative with probability \(\dfrac{20}{30}\) and positive with probability \(\dfrac{10}{30}\)
